complete.problem: Find the arc length and sector area of a 60 degree sector of radius 6 cm. The sector fraction is 60/360 = 1/6. Arc length = 1/6 x 2 pi x 6 = 2 pi, about 6.28 cm. Sector area = 1/6 x pi x 6 squared = 6 pi, about 18.8 square centimetres. Check the trap: the sector area is NOT half of anything to do with doubling - it is the same 1/6 fraction applied to the full circle area.
complete.selfExplanation: Explain why the same 1/6 fraction gives both the arc length and the sector area, naming the whole each one is a fraction of.

paired.problem: Find the volume of a square pyramid whose base is 6 cm by 6 cm and whose vertical height is 4 cm.
paired.solution: Pyramid volume is 1/3 x base area x height = 1/3 x 36 x 4 = 48 cubic centimetres.
